result.title: Scaling Laws for SAE Training Data
result.summary: Activation storage is often a bottleneck in sparse autoencoder (SAE) training. We study how many unique activations an SAE needs when its total training budget is fixed. Quality improves rapidly as the buffer grows, then reaches a plateau where replaying the buffer is nearly as effective as using fresh activations throughout training. Beyond this point, additional unique activations bring little benefit to reconstruction or interpretability, so the buffer need not grow with the training budget. We describe this tradeoff between diversity and repetition with a scaling law for limited data. We validate it across dictionary sizes and token budgets, early, middle, and late layers of Llama-3.1, Qwen3 model sizes, and BatchTopK, TopK, and JumpReLU SAEs. Sweeps using mathematical text and Python code test the effect of changing the activation source. Evaluation covers explained variance (EV), reconstruction MSE, feature absorption, automated interpretability, and sparse probing. These results give a practical training rule: choose the smallest buffer that reaches the quality plateau and replay it for the remaining budget. In our experiments, this reduces activation storage by $8\text{--}64\times$ with negligible quality loss.

AI.brief_summary: 研究固定训练预算下 SAE 需要多少独特激活：质量随缓冲区增大快速提升后进入平台，重放旧激活几乎等同使用新激活，据此给出多样性-重复的有限数据 scaling law，并在 Llama-3.1、Qwen3 多层、多种 SAE 变体上用 EV、MSE、特征吸收、自动解释性与稀疏探测验证，报告存储可降低 8–64 倍。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「独特数据量与重复的权衡及质量平台」可能为 latent 推理中需要多少不同推理状态、状态缓存与重放的预算分配提供可核查的类比与指标，但与视觉推理主线尚无直接联系。
